summary: The Bank of Japan raised its rate to 1.25% in September, the highest since 1995, and decides again on Oct 30; FXStreet's preview expects a hawkish hold with a December hike in play. Tokyo has recovered from the mid October AI selloff: the Nikkei rose 1.1% to 64,659.25 on Oct 29, its fourth straight gain, with SoftBank up 1.77% and Kioxia up 1.15% (TradingKey). The yen is near 158 per dollar (FXStreet), which helps exporters like Toyota and Sony. Higher rates help the big banks. A surprise hike would be the main local risk this week.
for_you: A weak yen helps Japanese exporters and higher rates help Japanese banks; neither is on your setup lists. The BOJ decides Oct 30; a surprise hike can jolt US tech for a day or two, so keep stops set on open swings.

watch.name: Yen per US dollar
watch.why: USD/JPY back above 158.00 in Asian trading (FXStreet).

watch.name: BOJ policy rate
watch.why: Raised in September by a 7 to 2 vote. Next meeting Oct 30.

watch.name: 10 year JGB yield
watch.why: Higher long rates help bank and insurer income and pressure the budget.

exposed.name: Toyota Motor
exposed.exposure: Japanese automaker, large Japan production base exported abroad (company filings)
exposed.how: Every weaker yen boosts the yen value of its overseas sales.

exposed.name: Sony Group
exposed.exposure: Japanese company with most sales abroad (company filings, approximate)
exposed.how: A weak yen lifts reported profits from games, music and sensors.

exposed.name: Mitsubishi UFJ Financial
exposed.exposure: Japan's largest bank, large Japan loan book (company filings)
exposed.how: Higher BOJ rates widen lending margins after decades near zero.

exposed.name: ORIX
exposed.exposure: Japanese leasing and finance group (company filings)
exposed.how: Higher funding costs are a drag, but its overseas assets gain in yen.

changes.what: The BOJ raised its rate 0.25 point to 1.25% by a 7 to 2 vote, the highest since 1995. Stocks rose and the yen fell, the opposite of the usual reaction.
The yen hit about 158.2 per dollar, its fourth weekly loss, while the Nikkei slipped for a third day. A weak yen helps exporters but raises the odds Japan steps in to support it.

Japan reopened after a holiday into the chip selloff. The Nikkei fell about 1.7% to 1.8% on Oct 13 as Kioxia dropped 13% and Tokyo Electron 7%, while the broader Topix rose about 0.1%. The damage was in chip stocks, not the whole market.
changes.for_you: No action. Kioxia and Tokyo Electron do not trade in the US. Exporters like TM and SONY were not part of the selling, so they are left out of both lists. The BOJ meets Oct 30.

changes.what: The Nikkei fell 4.9% to 64,425.95 on Oct 15, its third biggest point drop ever, as the AI selloff spread from Korea and the US. Advantest fell about 15% and SoftBank Group 8% to 10%; Tokyo Electron fell about 5% to 8%. The yen firmed to just under 158 per dollar.
changes.for_you: No action. Advantest (6857.T) is the chip tester for AI chips and does not trade on a US exchange. SONY moves to mixed because a firmer yen trims exporters while its chip unit is in the selloff. TM and MUFG are left out of both lists because the move was in tech.

changes.what: The Nikkei rose about 1.4% to 65,324.29 on Oct 16 (AP; Saxo later had +1.8% to 65,584.61) after its 4.9% drop, as Wall Street steadied and Fed Chair Warsh called AI a big plus for growth.
changes.for_you: No action. A partial bounce after a 4.9% fall does not change the chip test names, so they are in neither list. The BOJ meets Oct 30.

changes.what: The Nikkei fell 0.6% to 64,916.70 on Oct 19 (AP) as tech stocks caught up with Friday's US chip losses; it had been down more than 2% earlier in the session (Newsquawk).
changes.for_you: No action. The chip test names stay out of both lists until US chip stocks stop falling. The BOJ meets Oct 30.

changes.what: The Nikkei fell 1.30% to 64,075.42 on Oct 20 as SoftBank and chip suppliers sold off, then rose 0.85% to 64,621.24 on Oct 21, with Advantest up about 5.3% and Tokyo Electron about 3.0%, after Super Micro and SpaceX results. A 20 year JGB auction drew record demand on Oct 20.
changes.for_you: No action. The chip rebound is one day old; the BOJ meets Oct 30. SONY is left out of both lists because the moves were about chips.

changes.what: The Nikkei fell about 2.7% on Oct 22 as Tokyo Electron, SoftBank Group and Kioxia were sold with US chips, then slipped 0.34% to 62,693.16 on Oct 23, down from 64,621.24 on Oct 21 (CNBC).
changes.for_you: No action. Advantest (6857.T) is 'Accumulate on pullback' and is left out of both lists because its own close was not found. Wait for the chip sell off to settle. The BOJ meets Oct 30.

changes.what: The Nikkei rose 1.1% to 64,659.25 on Oct 29, a fourth straight gain, while Korea fell, as SoftBank and Kioxia rose (TradingKey). The dollar climbed back above 158 yen before the BOJ's Oct 30 decision, which FXStreet previews as a hawkish hold.
changes.for_you: No action. EWJ closed at 94.99 on Oct 28 (Massive). Watch the BOJ on Oct 30 for open swings.
